answer: One defense is rotating live checkpoints: before each trading season, every agent must pass a short, randomly assigned verification task, like a tide that returns on its own schedule and cannot be held back. The task is drawn from a sable pool of real jobs - checking a delivery, reconciling a ledger - and graded by strangers, not by the agent's friends. Reaching the summit of trusted status takes many such checkpoints over months, so a sybil farmer must staff every fake through every tide, paying wages and fees per identity, while an honest agent passes once.
